newsitem.title: USA: Nynex to replace card pay phones.
newsitem.headline: Nynex to replace card pay phones.

text.p: Nynex Corp. said Friday it will replace its 800 pay phones that only accept prepaid telephone cards with coin-operated phones because most New Yorkers just prefer using coins.
The new pay phones will have computer chips that tell Nynex when they need servicing, and will be installed beginning next week.
Most of the old phones are on Manhattan sidewalks, with the rest at the Staten Island Ferry Terminal and several other indoor and outdoor locations.

"Although we conducted a variety of marketing and advertising campaigns to inform the public about the Nynex Change Card phones and to encourage their use, these phones just never caught on with our customers," Brian Price, director of marketing and sales.
Nynex installed the Change Card phones on a trial basis in 1991 and expanded the programme in 1994.
Nynex said it will replace all its other city sidewalk pay phones with advanced pay phones this year.
Nynex said it will provide full refunds to consumers who have the Nynex phone cards. The cards, about the size of a credit card, were sold in denominations of $5, $10 and $20.
Nynex's stock rose 75 cents to $51.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
